steps.title: Still Doing Great
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes care with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask about a few other areas?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Returning: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to {{complaint_reference}}. First, can I ask about a few other areas?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name.)

Do you have any nagging joint pain?

Any heel or foot pain?

Any tendon trouble?

Is an old injury bothering you?

Do you have any muscle knots?

Any neck or back soreness?

Have you cut back on any activities?

Of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Returning: Check Other Areas
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name.)

Do you have any nagging joint pain?

Any heel or foot pain?

Any tendon trouble?

Is an old injury bothering you?

Do you have any muscle knots?

Any neck or back soreness?

Have you cut back on any activities?

Between those and the area returning, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask three quick questions about {{main_concern}}.

(Ask each question in order. Let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer.)

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer.)

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. Repeat back whatever they name.)

Thank you for sharing that. It helps us understand what is going on.

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can look at {{main_concern}}. We can see whether acoustic wave therapy may help. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. What is holding you back from having {{main_concern}} checked?

(Stay easy about it. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why They Stopped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad you're still doing well.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Do not argue with it.)

Acoustic wave therapy supports healing, but everyday strain can bring problems back. Regular checks help us catch changes early.

(Tap the reason they gave.)

steps.title: They Felt Fine
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When you feel good, coming back stops feeling urgent. Regular checks help us see whether the area is still doing well.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a check-in on the schedule. Would that be okay?

steps.title: They Mention Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. A check-in is one visit to see how the area is holding. You're not agreeing to more treatment.

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get that check-in scheduled. Does that seem fair?

steps.title: Life Got Busy
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and appointments get pushed down the list. We can find a time that works around your schedule.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's find an easy time for a check-in. Would that work?

steps.title: Waiting for Pain
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Pain can return after the area has been under strain for a while. A check may catch changes before they bother you.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's schedule a quick check. Is that okay?

steps.title: They Moved or Switched
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're nearby, we'd be glad to see you again. Your treatment history is already in your file.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a check-in scheduled. Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Fully Back: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to {{complaint_reference}}. First, can I ask about a few other areas?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Fully Back: Check Other Areas
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name.)

Do you have any nagging joint pain?

Any heel or foot pain?

Any tendon trouble?

Is an old injury bothering you?

Do you have any muscle knots?

Any neck or back soreness?

Have you cut back on any activities?

Between those and the area fully back, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Objection: “I thought it was fixed”
steps.content:
That's a fair thing to bring up. Everyday strain can bother an area again. A visit lets us see what changed.

Can we get you in for a look?

steps.title: Objection: “It came back”
steps.content:
That can happen after sessions stop. The area still deals with everyday strain. We should look at what changed before suggesting a plan.

Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Objection: “I manage it myself”
steps.content:
I understand. Home care may help for a while. A visit lets us check why {{main_concern}} keeps bothering you.

Is there anything else on your mind?

steps.title: Objection: Injections or Surgery
steps.content:
That's an important decision. A visit can show whether acoustic wave therapy is another option for you. Then you can compare your choices.

Would that information help?

(Wait for the answer.)

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. What part would you like to think over?

(Listen. Tap the closest reason if they name one.)

The visit gives you information about {{main_concern}}. Then you can decide what feels right.

Does that help?

steps.title: Objection: “Send me information”
steps.content:
I'd be glad to send information, {{contact_first_name}}. General information cannot show what is happening with {{main_concern}}. A visit gives you answers about your situation.

Could we schedule that first?
